item.title: Army to detonate tons of lead azide after delays. And, Abrego Garcia leaves U.S.
item.description: Authorities have evacuated a 5-mile radius to prepare to dispose of thousands of pounds of lead azide. And, after a nearly two-year legal battle, Kilmar Abrego Garcia's has voluntarily left the U.S.

item.description: Climbing tall mountains like Kilimanjaro is a study in contrasts — from beating sun to freezing nights, fire and snow.

item.title: Buying new things feels wonderful. But it can also be a trap
item.description: Constantly buying new things can be problematic, says journalist Eric Athas, author of the new book "Saying No to New." Here's how to break the cycle and find joy in what you already have.

item.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaves U.S. voluntarily for Spain
item.description: Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran immigrant who became a symbol of Trump's mass deportation campaign, voluntarily left the country on Tuesday after nearly two years of legal battles.

item.title: Africa Cup title given back to Senegal after sports court rules against Morocco
item.description: Senegal won the Africa Cup on the field in Morocco in January and then lost it in a legal case in March because its players walked off the field in protest in second-half stoppage time.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: These deer walk 300 miles a year. The race is on to save their migration
item.description: Mule deer in Wyoming make some of the longest land migrations in the lower 48 states. They're trying to adapt to a changing climate, but growing development could stand in their way.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: How tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs are squeezing the U.S.'s biggest apple region
item.description: Washington's $9 billion industry grows more than 70% of the nation's fresh apples. Farmers are being pressed by high costs, tariffs and a strong dollar that diminishes foreign purchasing power.
